items.summary: Databricks announced that Lakebase Postgres is now generally available on Google Cloud, letting teams run serverless, production-grade PostgreSQL directly within its Data + AI Platform. The offering combines compute and storage to cut infrastructure overhead and remove the ETL pipelines traditionally needed when merging operational data with analytics. KaBuM! cited it as a low-latency memory layer for its conversational AI agents. It is available across Google Cloud regions from launch, with no infrastructure or pipelines to manage.},
items.title: Databricks Makes Lakebase Postgres Generally Available on Google Cloud

items.summary: Apple’s new CEO John Ternus is reportedly advancing household robot development, with the first product possibly being an autonomous home robot that supports FaceTime calls and controls lights. People who worked on Apple’s robotic projects told The Information it could be named HomeView Ultra, code-named J595, priced at $1,000 or more by 2027—though delays may push the launch to 2028. Critics note its reported features seem underwhelming versus existing smart home devices.
items.title: Apple’s New CEO Pushes a $1,000 Home Robot Targeting 2027

items.summary: Last week Anthropic introduced a system prompt to stop its Claude models from recreating specific existing video games. The change, spotted by user chasm and verified by XDA in binary version 2.1.314 released October 30, allows original or genre games but bars exact reproductions. Engineer Addy Osmani confirmed the addition on social media.
items.title: Anthropic's Claude rules may not curb AI game copying wave

items.summary: The MIT Energy Initiative held its annual research conference on Sept. 22-23 under the theme “Transitioning energy at a pivotal moment,” drawing more than 200 attendees in person and online. Paula Hammond of the MIT School of Engineering opened with remarks stressing an interdisciplinary approach to decarbonization, while keynote speaker Eric Toone of Breakthrough Energy argued that prosperity now depends on cutting emissions. Sessions covered nuclear revival, carbon utilization, startup commercialization, early-stage research, quantum computing at Quantum@MIT led by Danna Freedman, and the energy demands of AI data centers. Steve Clemmer cited an analysis showing hyperscale facilities could be 10 to even 10,000 times larger than a decade ago, raising costs and climate damages; Larry Susskind urged developers to earn community trust through benefits agreements.
items.title: MIT Energy Initiative Conference Explores Decarbonization, AI and Quantum

items.summary:
Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE malware botnet of more than 1.3 million Android TV streaming boxes that Google says its manufacturer intentionally infected to generate revenue through cybercrime. The company attributes the infection with high confidence to Chinese maker Videostrong Technology Co, accusing it of installing a persistent backdoor into device firmware and selling access to criminal affiliates used for ad fraud, residential proxies, and other malware. Google terminated its relationship with Videostrong, revoked its license to manufacture certified Android devices, and banned future affiliates from producing them. Synthient traced the malware after finding it preinstalled on a MECOOL box purchased in late 2025. Although operations were disrupted, the backdoor remains on infected devices unless clean firmware is installed or they are disconnected online.

visual null
items.title: Google Takedowns Million-Device XCPE Android Botnet, Bans TV Box Maker

items.summary: ZDNET reports that OpenAI will merge the chat and work tabs of its ChatGPT desktop app starting in December 2025, according to a note on OpenAI's website. The integrated experience will be tested with select users before wider rollout, which OpenAI says should not disrupt most customers' usage resets or workflows.
items.title: OpenAI Merges ChatGPT Chat and Work Tabs in December

items.summary: Over Halloween weekend, some Grok Bot users found their weekly usage limits unexpectedly maxed out. Users reported on X that usage jumped from as low as 50% to 100%. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk confirmed in an X post on Sunday that this was not a glitch, writing that serving costs were unsustainably high relative to revenue. He has not addressed the issue further or explained how limits will change.
items.title: Musk Cuts Grok Bot Limits Over High Costs

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Athenahealth, a US healthcare technology provider serving over 20% of the population, launched an MCP-compatible server called AthenaPatient MCP connecting patient health records to Anthropic's Claude. The tool is available only to Claude Pro and Max users, costing $20 and $100 per month respectively. Patients must sign in with their credentials, choose what data to share, and can revoke access anytime. Sam Lambson of Athenahealth said the partnership does not provide medical advice.
items.title: Athenahealth Lets Patients Ask Claude About Their Records

items.summary: Ray announced today a new Special Interest Group (SIG) dedicated to hardware accelerators, marking what the announcement calls a crucial time to build on Ray's foundation. When Ray was created at UC Berkeley over 10 years ago, distributed computing meant CPU clusters running frameworks like Apache Hadoop and Spark; GPUs were only just entering machine learning. Today accelerated computing is central to AI development and deployment. The public interest group will bring together hardware vendors, contributors, and developers to define a shared, vendor-neutral roadmap covering three core areas: Development and Testing Infrastructure, Hardware Awareness Capabilities, and Networking/Transport.
items.title: Ray Announces Special Interest Group for Hardware Accelerators

items.summary: Google published a roundup of the artificial intelligence news it announced in October 2026. The company said teams across Google were working on applications spanning healthcare, crisis response, and education. It released Gemini 4 Argon for complex coding, financial analysis, legal workflows, robotics reasoning, and physical-world tasks, then two weeks later introduced Gemini 4 Carbon as its strongest model yet for cybersecurity and long-horizon engineering; Carbon is in pre-release testing with the U. S. government and trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program before a broader launch.
items.title: Google reviews its October AI announcements, from Gemini models to quantum and space milestones

items.summary: Authors Jason Pielemeier, Jhalak M. Kakkar, Elonnai Hickok, and Sudisha Mishra Revati Vaidya examine how five leading AI developers — Anthropic, Google (Alphabet), Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI — envision public governance of frontier models as part of the MAP-AI project. The firms disagree sharply on pacing: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls for a new FAA-style agency to block risky releases, while Mark Zuckerberg rejects prerelease review, offering partly trained models and staff instead. Others converge on publishing safety frameworks, testing against risk domains, independent audits, transparency reporting, early government access, and antitrust waivers — though Meta stays silent on external audits.
items.title: Five AI Firms Sketch Divergent Paths for Public Governance of Frontier Models

items.summary: Singapore's manufacturing activity expanded at a slower pace in October, with the purchasing managers' index falling to 51.4 points from 51.7 in September. The electronics sector PMI dropped to 52.5 from 52.9, weighed down by weaker new orders and rising input costs. Analysts caution that momentum may be pausing rather than reversing amid Middle East shipping disruptions, while Oxford Economics raised its GDP forecast for 2026 to 5.7% but flagged electronics demand as a risk.
items.title: Singapore Factory Growth Slows in October as New Orders Weaken

items.summary: In a Forum piece, Liu Fook Thim welcomed the rollout of vending machines selling local vegetables under $2 but argued that matching supply with sustained consumer demand at competitive prices is harder. He noted reported prices of $1. 40 to $1. 80 per pack through SG Farmers’ Market versus at least $2 for leafy greens at FairPrice, and said supermarket prices are about 43% higher than the lowest stated vending-machine price. He cautioned that this comparison does not establish margins or account for imported produce, which should be the benchmark.
items.title: Commentator questions cost of local vegetable vending machines in Singapore

items.summary: Darius Lee writes in The Straits Times Forum that Singapore should gazette more public holidays, calling them legally mandated rest. He notes the country has 11 gazetted holidays, fewer than Malaysia's 16 or Indonesia's 27, and unchanged since 1968 when they were cut from 16 to 11 as part of urging citizens to work harder amid departing British troops. Then Law and National Development Minister E. W.
items.title: Singaporean writer urges more public holidays as a promised rest

items.summary: Regina Barzilay and James Collins of MIT received the 2026 Pritzker Prize for AI in Science Research Excellence for pioneering AI-enabled antibiotic discovery. Their work, including identifying halicin through a deep learning model trained on 2,500 molecules, accelerated drug-resistant bacteria research from years to weeks. Both researchers emphasized that AI automates parts of discovery rather than fully transforming it.
items.title: MIT Researchers Win Pritzker Prize for AI Antibiotic Discovery Work

items.summary: Alstom cut its full-year guidance after delays in key German projects, including Coradia Max orders from states such as Baden-Wurttemberg and Lower Saxony, led to penalties that hurt margins. Shares slumped about 27% on Nov 2. The company now expects an adjusted Ebit margin of about 1%, down from 6. 5%, a cash burn of €1. 5 billion instead of positive free cash flow, and train car production of about 4,000 units from 4,500. It plans to slash debt by about €2 billion through divestments amid an organisational review.
items.title: Alstom Cuts Guidance and Announces Overhaul After German Project Delays

items.summary: The article explains how Nvidia built its Nemotron family of large language models, focusing on techniques that lower computation and memory use while keeping capacity. It describes the transformer-based generation process, then details two cost-reducing methods: Mamba layers with a fixed numerical state to avoid quadratic growth in attention work, and mixture-of-experts routing where only part of the model activates per token. Nemotron 3 Super has about 120 billion total parameters and 12 billion active; Ultra scales to roughly 550 billion total and 55 billion active. Nvidia also uses BF16 weights (about 16 bits) and its NVFP4 format, which combines four-bit values with scaling information plus quantization-aware distillation. Using these methods, the model size dropped from about 66 GB for BF16 to about 22 GB for the NVFP4 checkpoint. The post notes it is based on publicly shared details and invites corrections.
items.title: Nvidia Explains How Nemotron Cuts Model Costs

items.summary: Supermarkets across Europe have been hit by a suspected cyber-attack affecting their fridges and freezers, prompting concern about the security of internet-connected devices. Experts say manufacturers must improve device safety, while UK law now requires certain smart-device makers to meet minimum standards since April 2024.
items.title: Suspected cyber-attack on European supermarket fridges raises wider hardware-security fears

items.summary: A report by MIT Technology Review’s custom content arm examines the quality of insights produced by agentic AI in enterprise analytics. Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at surveyed organizations lead to business improvement, though this rose from 37% a year earlier. While descriptive insights are praised, prescriptive ones draw mixed reviews. The main causes cited include insufficient business context and fragmented data.
items.title: MIT Technology Review Report on Agentic Analytics Insight Quality

items.summary: The New York Times sued privacy-focused browser maker Brave on Monday, alleging it scraped and distributed the outlet’s copyrighted content to AI companies including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere. The Daily News, Chicago Tribune, and Orlando Sentinel filed similar suits in Manhattan federal court. The complaint calls Brave a distributor of stolen content.
items.title: Publishers Sue Brave Over Content Scraping

items.summary: Two new reports argue that a methane measurement method called global warming potential, or GWP*, lets livestock-heavy countries hide real emissions. A Greenpeace-commissioned analysis of the top 10 livestock exporters found they could cut actual methane by only 0.6 percent yet report a 30 percent reduction under GWP*. The gap equals about 1,538 million metric tons of carbon dioxide in one year. Separately, researchers at UCLA found beef meals measured as roughly 3,500 grams under the standard method but more than 7,000 grams over 20 years. Campaigners call it creative accounting that weakens climate goals.
items.title: Greenpeace Report Criticizes GWP* Methane Accounting

items.summary: Carbon Brief has produced an interactive table analysing around 100 documents on positions ahead of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. The site notes Australia leads negotiations while Turkey hosts and pushes its own action agenda covering electrification, oceans and green industrialisation. Topics include a just transition mechanism agreed at COP30 but still lacking details, contested climate finance under Article 9.1, adaptation versus mitigation priorities, and nationally determined contributions. As of the writing, only 150 parties responsible for three-quarters of global emissions have submitted new NDCs by 2025, while a joint letter from 105 parties called for putting oceans at the heart of climate action. The table is described as a living document to be updated over COP31.
items.title: Carbon Brief Maps Positions Ahead of COP31 Climate Talks

items.summary: John Ashford and Jared Dubnow of The Hawthorn Group examine the growing political backlash against data centers ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. They report that public sentiment has shifted substantially, citing an October POLITICO poll conducted by PF Global showing half of Americans now oppose a data center built within three miles of their homes, up from 28% in January. The strategists say this opposition is already influencing state and federal policy, pointing to actions by Texas Governor Greg Abbott and Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, as well as Public Service Commission races in Georgia. They assert that data center regulation will persist regardless of election outcomes and warn developers of emerging technologies like small modular reactors may underestimate how quickly public attitudes can change.
items.title: Public Affairs Strategists Warn Data Center Backlash Could Reshape Power Policy

items.summary: Anthropic reported a more than 1,100 per cent surge in quarterly revenue as it prepares for its Wall Street listing later this month. Third-quarter revenue reached US$17 billion, up from US$1.4 billion a year earlier. The company's amended filing showed net loss of US$23.3 billion, mostly from non-cash accounting charges tied to rising valuation, and an operating loss of US$567 million as it paid more for computing capacity.
items.title: Anthropic Reports Revenue Surge Ahead of IPO

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet began selling €6 billion ($6.7 billion) of bonds on Monday, according to a memo from one deal's managers, testing investor appetite after AI-related doubts triggered tech selloffs and its worst-ever share drop last Thursday. The offering spans seven tranches with demand just over €17 billion; proceeds may repay debt as the company expects up to $205 billion in annual capital spending.
items.title: Alphabet Opens €6 Billion Bond Sale Amid Tech Debt Concerns

items.summary: Amazon listed a 128GB iPhone 16 at ₹76,999, down from an MRP of Rs 89,900, giving a direct discount of ₹12,901 or roughly 14%. Additional offers may lower the effective cost further: up to ₹5,000 off with HDFC Bank credit cards and cashback of up to ₹2,309 through Amazon Pay Balance. However, these benefits may not all combine, and final savings depend on buyer eligibility and the exchanged phone's condition.
items.title: Amazon's iPhone 16 Diwali deal hides extra savings in fine print

items.summary: This NBER working paper by Babbar, Kantor, Whalley and Zeng uses patent data from 1947 to 1992. It shows NASA-sponsored patents were more automation-intensive than non-NASA ones in the same classes. Industries near Space Race activity saw persistent labor-share declines but little change in skill mix.
items.title: NASA R&D pushed US manufacturing toward automation, study finds

items.summary: David Baqaee, Ariel Burstein and Joao Guerreiro study optimal monetary policy in a heterogeneous-agent model where the policymaker maximizes joint household surplus rather than social welfare. They find that when labor wedges are homogeneous, policy matches the standard benchmark; departures arise from heterogeneity, raising output-gap stabilization weight by about 37 percent.
items.title: Policymakers Maximize Household Surplus in New Model

items.summary: British Gas has resumed force-fitting prepayment meters in homes of customers who cannot afford their energy bills, months after paying the largest settlement on record over debt collectors entering vulnerable households. The regulator lifted an almost four-year block following a settlement worth more than £100m extracted during the Russian gas crisis. Forced fittings remain banned for young children and people over 75. Campaigners warn the timing adds winter stress; British Gas defends its plan as household energy debt is forecast to exceed £7bn, adding around £80 to average bills.
items.title: Ofgem Clears British Gas to Resume Forced Prepayment Meters

items.summary: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood scaled back her strictest migration plans following a cabinet backlash, offering care workers an exemption to apply for indefinite leave to remain after five years. Most other rigorous changes remain, including long waits of up to 30 years for those arriving by irregular means. Home Office officials estimate about 500,000 migrants will wait longer than the current five years, though critics note 1.4 million out of 1.9 million 'Boriswave' legal migrants would still qualify after five years. The Law Society and business groups warned the retrospective rules could undermine certainty and cost businesses. Andy Burnham endorsed the earned-element approach while opposition figures condemned it as capitulation.
items.title: Mahmood softens immigration settlement rules after cabinet revolt

items.summary: The writer found both Fjord and Fatherland worth watching, noting that the Romanian director Cristian Mungiu won the Golden Prize at Cannes for Fjord. He judged its right-wing message heavy-handed but called it a quality film. For Fatherland, his Polish take on postwar Germany, he praised how convincingly it portrayed East German communism in about an hour and twenty-two minutes, though he said it demands knowledge of German history, literature, and culture.
items.title: A filmgoer weighs two Cannes-adjacent movies on politics and history

items.summary: A cyber-attack targeting refrigerators and freezers forced dozens of supermarkets across several European countries to dump large quantities of spoiled food. Belgium and Luxemburg saw the worst damage, with 40 Delhaize supermarkets affected, while incidents also occurred in stores across Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. In a Hoeilaart branch near Brussels, frozen pizzas and ice cream were found among rubbish. The damaged store estimated costs at more than €100,000 (£83,500).
items.title: European supermarkets discard food after freezer cyber-attack

items.summary: A columnist examines how Democrats are weighing aggressive legal and investigative tactics against President Donald Trump’s administration as they approach the midterm elections. The piece opens with a story about Mike Doyle, an Alaska Democrat who ran under a confusing name to expose Republican meddling in a 2018 race — but notes that no federal investigation followed. It then traces how the debate over “lawfare” has evolved since 2016 and through the Trump years, citing figures such as six ongoing Russia investigations after Biden replaced Trump. Quotes from Robert Garcia and Gov. Josh Shapiro frame calls for new norms. The author concludes Democrats face pressure to act while voters decide their appetite for it. Attribution remains tied throughout: findings are presented in the columnist’s voice; quotes carry named speakers; forecasts use hedged language like “I’d expect.” No independent verification is claimed beyond what the article states.
items.title: Democrats Consider Lawfare Tactics Against Trump Ahead of Midterm Senate Race

items.summary: German news magazine Der Spiegel reported that Apple sent spyware threat warnings to members of a delegation accompanying Chancellor Friedrich Merz on his recent trip to Singapore, Japan and South Korea. The alerts reached ministry staff and journalists as well. Government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said the federal government is taking the incident very seriously while authorities investigate possible device compromise.
items.title: Apple Warns German Officials of Possible Spyware Breach After Merz Asia Trip

items.summary: Oracle filed Monday plans to raise $20 billion through stock and bond sales, seeking $10 billion in common stock and an equal amount in senior notes. The company said proceeds could fund capital expenditures, debt repayments or future investments, though neither offering had been priced at filing. Oracle has capped additional fundraising at $20 billion through fiscal 2030, split evenly between equity and debt, excluding refinancing borrowings. It expects capital spending to peak during fiscal 2027 and 2028 before financing growth internally from fiscal 2029. Shares fell about 4.5% after the announcement.
items.title: Oracle Files $20 Billion Capital-Raise Plan for AI Data-Center Growth

items.summary: President Donald Trump notified Congress he intends to remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) preferential trade programme, effective 1 January 2027. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said an annual review found both countries engaged in practices inconsistent with eligibility requirements. The administration cited barriers to trade, national security concerns, corruption, human rights issues, and strained relations between Washington and the two nations.
items.title: Trump Notifies Congress of Removing Rwanda and South Africa from AGOA Trade Program

items.summary: At least 26 people were killed when Russian bombs struck an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha, southern Zaporizhzhia. Regional head Mykhailo Semikin said nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village and that people remained under the rubble. President Volodymyr Zelensky called the attack "utterly horrific" and later said 26 deaths were confirmed. Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS had earlier reported 24 killed, including two rescuers and four police officers. The Russian military has not commented.
items.title: Zelensky Condemns Russian Bombing That Killed 26 at Aid Centre

items.summary: Researchers analysing hind leg bones of an Aratasaurus, which lived about 115m years ago and is held at the National Museum of Brazil since its 2008 discovery, claim to have found structures resembling fossilised red blood cells plus heme. Prof Kliti Grice calls it a world first that could open new avenues for studying dinosaur biology. The finding remains controversial; Prof Mary Schweitzer doubts the shapes are true red blood cells and stresses more study is needed.
items.title: Scientists report fossilised red blood cells in a dinosaur bone

items.summary: Savannah Guthrie posted a new appeal for information about her mother Nancy Guthrie, who authorities believe was abducted from their Tucson home on 1 February. Sharing photos of an old drawing and her mother’s image with emotional captions, she said the family “cannot move forward” and asked others to share what they know. A $1m reward remains; investigators have found blood drops and a discredited glove but no arrests.
items.title: Guthrie Issues New Plea in Mother's Abduction Case

items.summary: On the eve of US midterm elections, President Donald Trump's administration is seeking a Supreme Court injunction to sideline over 20,000 mail-in ballots in California, claiming non-US citizens are attempting to vote. The Justice Department, run by former personal attorney Todd Blanche, says it has a list documenting alleged ineligible voters compiled by the Department of Homeland Security. A district court judge rejected an earlier request, warning singling out ballots would harm voter trust.
items.title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Block California Ballots

items.summary: Josh Addo-Carr's playing future with the Parramatta Eels is undecided as he awaits a club decision. His B-sample from a roadside drugs test returned negative, so police will take no further action. He met Eels officials at a Monday board meeting to respond to a breach notice. His lawyer said he remains committed to the club.
items.title: Addo-Carr's Parramatta future hinges on club decision after negative B-sample

items.summary: Australia's Reserve Bank is widely expected today to lift the cash rate for a fifth time this year, to an 18-year high of 4.85 per cent, after senior officials warned inflation remained too high. The board will vote at 2:30pm AEDT, with governor Michele Bullock speaking afterward.
items.title: RBA Expected to Hike Cash Rate to 18-Year High of 4.85%

items.summary: A Brazilian federal court ordered non-Indigenous occupants, employees and their property out of the Piripkura Indigenous Territory in Mato Grosso within 120 days. The ruling follows evidence of illegal deforestation and cattle ranching, including a recent inspection identifying 36.83 hectares (91 acres) of unauthorized clearing attributed to one rancher. It reverses an earlier decision that let some occupants stay until demarcation concluded under the Marco Temporal law, which Brazil's Supreme Court struck down in Dec. 2025. A judge set a daily fine of 500 Brazilian reais (about $93) for non-compliance; Funai may enforce removal with police if needed. Prosecutors say voluntary departure remains the priority to avoid contact with isolated Indigenous people, who have lived there since demarcation was first proposed over 40 years ago.
items.title: Brazil Court Orders Ranchers Out of Isolated Piripkura Territory

items.summary: Supermarket refrigeration systems across Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden saw temperature spikes on Monday, forcing retailers to discard spoilt produce. The incident follows an October attack in France that affected hundreds of shops. Cybersecurity specialists told AFP that industrial equipment once run offline is now commonly connected online for remote monitoring, creating a route for attackers to disrupt physical systems.
items.title: European supermarkets hit by fresh wave of refrigeration cyberattacks

items.summary: Actor Michael C. Hall, now 55, discusses the 20th anniversary of Dexter Morgan in a video-call interview promoting Dexter: Resurrection's recreated opening credits sequence. Introduced in October 2006 and running through 2013 before returning via New Blood (2021-2022), the Miami-based character now plays out in New York as Hall ages alongside him. Hall says the character has integrated his two sides, blurring the line between the forensic analyst and killer he once compartmentalized. Asked why Dexter remains popular, he notes people relate to managing their own inner darkness while watching him take control.
items.title: Michael C. Hall Reflects on Two Decades as Dexter Morgan

items.summary: A study published Oct. 22 in Nature Food introduces an index scoring 126 countries on their vulnerability to conflict between small-scale fishers and industrial vessels, which can threaten food security and livelihoods through competition for species, disputes over fishing grounds, or gear damage. Lead author Melissa Cronin of the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth told Mongabay that such conflicts are likely to increase as blue economy development expands. The index measures exposure based on nearshore industrial activity, small-scale catch intensity, and governance strength; West Africa ranked most vulnerable, with Guinea, Sierra Leone and Mozambique highest worldwide. Seto of UCSC called the study unique in its global reach but cautioned it does not assess policy effectiveness.
items.title: New Index Ranks Countries by Conflict Vulnerability in Fisheries

items.summary: Britain’s oldest cars took to the streets of London on Sunday, 1 November, for the annual London to Brighton Veteran Car Run. The 97km journey from Hyde Park to the south coast saw some vehicles travelling at just 12 to 20 mph. Shaun Harborne described his 1901 Renault Type D as fragile, while Karl-Heinz Jungbeck said it offered a taste of early motoring.
items.title: Veteran cars take part in London to Brighton run

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said deadly Russian strikes on an aid distribution centre in Zaporizhzhia dampened hopes of progress toward peace. The attack killed at least 24 people, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service (DSNS), and injured five others. Zelenskyy called it 'utterly horrific' and urged a strong response from the world.
items.title: Zelenskyy Blames Russian Strikes for Dampening Peace Hopes

items.summary: British adventurer Karl Bushby returned to his mother's home in Britain on Monday, reuniting with family. He had walked 50,000 kilometres from South America over a period described as lasting about two and three-quarters of a decade, crossing four continents.
items.title: Karl Bushby returns home after decades-long walk across four continents

items.summary: The Africanews weekly agenda reports that the death toll from the Democratic Republic of the Congo's 17th Ebola outbreak has exceeded 5,000. It also lists upcoming events: South Africa municipal elections on 4 November with over 2 million early voters; Kenya pastor Paul Mackenzie facing life imprisonment after his forced fasting killed 190 people; and Tanzania High Court ruling on opposition leader Tundu Lissu's treason charges on 6 November, alongside Pope Leo XIV's visit to Uruguay from 6 to 8 November. The agenda closes with a prompt to stay tuned to Africanews. com for more information.
items.title: Africanews Weekly Agenda Covers Ebola Toll and Key November Dates

items.summary: Buckingham Palace said King Charles III will address Britain's historical role in transatlantic slavery at a Commonwealth speech, pledging to do so 'with unflinching honesty and sincere sorrow.' The comments came as some Caribbean nations called for a formal state apology and financial reparations. The Palace stressed the king would respect wider government discussions and would not address matters of particular UK policy.
items.title: King Charles vows honest reckoning with Britain's slavery role

items.summary: A study in Current Biology examines an unusual relationship between a bull named Achille and a male donkey called Patroclo on an Ethiopian plateau. Researchers, who first noticed the pair while studying gelada monkeys, recorded 51 mounting attempts over four days, of which 34 involved penetration (s7). The authors note they cannot say how long the bond lasted or what evolutionary purpose it serves, since same-sex behaviour between males and females is not assumed to be default. Drawing on examples from bonobos and dolphins, they argue that sexual activity may strengthen social relationships even without producing offspring, urging scientists to question assumptions about natural sexuality rather than assign human identities to animals.
items.title: Study Explores Same-Sex Bond Between Ethiopian Bull and Donkey

items.summary: Anthropic reported a $567 million operating loss in the July-September quarter, with much of its net loss from non-cash valuation charges. Its amended IPO filing disclosed spending commitments of approximately $895 billion toward computing infrastructure, including $70 billion due before September 2027. The company is considering raising around $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion as it tests investor appetite for AI investments.
items.title: Anthropic's Revenue Surge and AI Spending Ahead of IPO

items.summary: PIB Fact Check has labelled a widely shared message as fake, clarifying that the Reserve Bank of India issued no announcement warning of a shortage of Rs 10, Rs 20 and Rs 50 notes ahead of Diwali. The viral circular, dated October 27, 2026, claimed inadequate supply during the festive season and urged people to use UPI, cards and net banking instead of cash. It also suggested printing was being reduced as part of a less-cash economy move. After the message circulated on WhatsApp, PIB shared its clarification on X, urging people to verify information against official RBI announcements before believing or sharing such messages.
items.title: Press Information Bureau Fact Check Debunks Viral Fake RBI Circular on Small-Denomination Notes

items.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday urged the Tata Group and Tata Trusts to resolve their differences through dialogue, calling it a sensitive matter given the group's significant contribution to the Indian economy. Speaking at the Financial Express Leadership Awards 2026 in New Delhi, she said disputes should be settled internally rather than spilling into public view, while declining to comment on government intervention or mediation.
items.title: Finance Minister Urges Tata Group and Trusts to Resolve Differences Through Dialogue

items.summary: The Indian Navy rescued all 20 crew members of fishing vessel Azini from armed pirates in a 48-hour operation in the Arabian Sea, with support from the Indian Air Force. The vessel was reportedly seized more than 3,000 km from Mumbai. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh praised the mission and reaffirmed India's commitment to safe seas.
items.title: Navy Rescues Fishing Vessel Crew From Pirates

items.summary: The Scottish National Party government handed a £35.4 million (£35,400,000) contract worth about Rs 450 crore to the Bengaluru-based company Mphasis to run Scotland’s benefits management platform serving roughly two million citizens. Opposition ministers Mark Griffin and Harriet Cross criticised the award as favouring overseas business over local jobs. The government says procurement followed equal-bid rules.
items.title: Scottish opposition criticises welfare IT contract awarded to Bengaluru firm

items.summary: The Supreme Court, through a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale, permitted the bursting of approved green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8 ahead of Diwali 2026. The relaxation follows concerns about implementing earlier pollution-control directions. Manufacturers must hold valid certifications from CSIR-NEERI and PESO and produce only listed crackers during a window of November 2–6, while traders whose licences were cancelled get temporary restoration until November 6. Crackers containing barium or joined in series are banned, and bursting is barred within 300 metres of hospitals, schools and silence zones. Bursts may occur from 6 am to 7 am and 8 pm to 10 pm only; the full ban returns on November 9. The court noted it lacked adequate data for a complete ban. Monitoring by CPCB and further hearings are set for December 16. Directions were reported via PTI, authored by Garvit Bhirani of LiveMint.
items.title: Supreme Court Allows Green Firecrackers in Delhi-NCR Ahead of Diwali

items.summary: Yelp released its first-ever list, ranking 100 Indian restaurants across the United States just ahead of Diwali and the fall season. The platform identified businesses under the Indian restaurant category using review volume and ratings, capping ten entries per state and requiring a passing health score as of August 11, 2026. California and Florida feature prominently, with LA Indian Cuisine taking first place amid more than 500 five-star reviews. Yelp's findings suggest diners are exploring beyond familiar dishes: searches for buffets near users surged 437% in 2026, while tiffin-service searches rose 76%, and butter chicken searches hit an all-time high in February 2026.
items.title: Yelp Releases First List of Top Indian Restaurants in the US

items.summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has directed telecom operators and internet service providers to run round-the-clock complaint centres handled by AI agents, with human assistance required for at least 16 hours a day. The rules also introduce penalties up to ₹20 lakh per quarter per service area for mishandled disputes, halved appeal timelines, quarterly reporting requirements, and oversight committees replacing advisory ones. TRAI cited rising complaints—73,081 in 2025-26 versus 44,733 in 2023-24—to justify the changes. Operators opposed round-the-clock operations on cost grounds; TRAI responded that it does not imply equal resources around the clock. The rules take effect after gazette publication and a phased rollout over up to 90 days.
items.title: TRAI Mandates AI Complaint Centres With Human Backup

items.summary: A Louisiana appeals court increased a homeowner's recovery after a $32,500 wooden bulkhead failed during a May 2017 flood and shifted her house. In Molbert v. Kenko Bulkhead & Marine Services, LLC (decided October 30, 2026), the Third Circuit removed Molbert's 25% share of fault after experts found improper design and construction caused the collapse with no homeowner negligence. The court raised mental anguish compensation from $7,500 to $15,000, dropped a $2,500 loss-of-enjoyment award, and revised damages so her total reached $448,431.34. It also held the insurer covered house damage but not bulkhead replacement costs, and rejected deducting her separate flood insurance payment.
items.title: Louisiana Court Boosts Homeowner's Recovery After Failed Flood Barrier

items.summary: Texas opened a new state park, Post Oak Ridge, on September 24, 2026. The roughly 3,118-acre property sits along the Colorado River in Central Texas and includes part of land once used by John Fletcher and Mattie Lou Vann for ranching from 1889. State Parks and Wildlife Department officials said development continues, with camping facilities expected around 2029. The park is among the first developed using interest from the $1 billion Centennial Parks Conservation Fund, which voters approved in 2023 to support new parks as recreation demand grows.
items.title: Texas Opens Post Oak Ridge State Park Backed by $1 Billion Conservation Fund
